Garuḍapurāṇa
or gAruDapurANa one of the 18 Mahāpurāṇas, revealed by Viṣṇu to Garuḍa an. imparted by him to Kaśyapa; also called Ādimahāpurāṇa (See NCC. II. p. 86b); mostly in two Khaṇḍas-Pūrva an. Uttara (also called Pretakalpa), except in a few mss. an. in Veṅk. edn. containing a third section known a. Brahmakāṇḍa; sometimes referred to a. Tārkṣya an. Sauparṇa; classified a. a Vaiṣṇavapurāṇa a. it devotes more attention to the worship of Viṣṇu than to that of other deities; current text probably compiled between 850 an. 1000 A. D.
See R. C. Hazra, ABORI. XIX. p.. 69-78 an. Studies in the Purāṇic Records on Hindu Rites an. Customs, p.. 142-43.
The text mentions its extent a. 8800 verses, which almost agrees with the number found in the ptd. edns. an. also with that given in Agni (a. 8000 verses); according to Matsya, Nārada an. Brahmavaivarta it had either 18000 or 19000 verses.
For the view that the extant purāṇa is apocryphal see R. C. Hazra, Studies in the Purāṇic Records on Hindu Rites an. Customs, p.. 142-143. [Page321-a.
The portion expressing advaitic ideas might have formed part of the older genuine text.
For a. analysis see Poona Ori. XXIII. iii-iv. p.. 22-38; IHQ. VI. p.. 553-60.
On the Rājanīti portion of its Bṛhaspatisaṁhitā an. Cāṇakyarājanītiśāstra, see ABORI. XXXVII. p.. 58-110; Ind.-Iran. Jour. I. iii. p.. 181-200. Also L. Sternbach, A New Abridged Version of the Bṛhaspatisaṁhitā of Garuḍapurāṇa, Purana Dept., AllIndia Kasiraja Trust, Varanasi, 1966.
For its section on gems see below, Ratnaparīkṣā.
A Study of the Purāṇa has been prepared by N. Gangadharan in the Dept. of Sanskrit, University of Madras an. submitted for a research degree.
